name: Lachen
tagline: The big pass: base for Gurudongmar and a Dzumsa village
meta_description: Lachen on a budget: base for Gurudongmar Lake, Lachen Monastery of 1858, the Dzumsa council, permits, room costs and current road status.
summary: Lachen is a Bhutia village at about 2,750 m on the Lachen Chu, 129 km from Gangtok, and the overnight base for Gurudongmar Lake and Chopta Valley. Like Lachung it is governed by its Dzumsa. Tours spend one night and leave for Gurudongmar at 3–4 am; two nights help with altitude. Check current status before you travel.

local_story.title: The council, the gompa and the 4 am convoy
paras: Lachen means big pass, and the valley above it leads to the high plateau and passes toward Tibet. Its people, the Lachenpas, are Bhutias who once moved between the village, the high summer pastures at Thangu and beyond, and trade over the border. The Dzumsa, the council of all households under an elected Pipon, has run village life since the first half of the 19th century, and still decides much of how tourism works here: which vehicles go, which homes take guests and how waste is handled.

Above the village stands Lachen Monastery, Ngodrub Choling, a Nyingma gompa built in 1858 that also runs a monastic school. In 1849 Joseph Dalton Hooker came up this valley toward the Kongra La, recording plants and people for his Himalayan Journals, before being detained with Archibald Campbell on a later stage of the journey. Lachen today is busiest before dawn: tour vehicles line up at 3–4 am for the climb to Gurudongmar, and by mid-morning the village is quiet again.

did_you_know: Lachen Monastery, also called Ngodrub Choling, was built in 1858 and runs the Lachen Monastic School.
Lachen and Lachung are the only villages in Sikkim governed by a Dzumsa instead of a gram panchayat.
In Lachen's high pastures, Dokpa yak herders keep their herds; the Lashar valley nearby is known for a yak race at their festival.
intro: Lachen is smaller, quieter and colder than Lachung. The village climbs a slope above the Lachen Chu, with wooden houses, a monastery at the top and a short main street of homestays and small hotels. For most visitors it is a place to sleep a few hours before the Gurudongmar run, but it repays a second night.

That second night matters. Gurudongmar is about 2,400 m higher than Lachen, and arriving from Gangtok in the evening and driving up at 4 am gives the body almost no time to adjust. A spare day lets you walk up to the gompa, visit Chopta Valley or simply rest, and then do the lake with less risk. Since 2023 the road between Chungthang and Lachen has closed for long periods; check current status before you travel.

highlights.title: Gurudongmar at dawn
highlights.text: The reason most travellers come: a 3–4 am departure, about 65 km and three hours to the sacred lake at about 5,180 m, back to Lachen for a late breakfast. Indians only; check current status before you travel.

highlights.title: Lachen Monastery
highlights.text: Ngodrub Choling, built in 1858, sits above the village with a monastic school attached. Walk up in the afternoon to hear young monks at lessons and look back over the valley. Donations welcome.

highlights.title: Chopta Valley
highlights.text: A high meadow valley near Thangu at about 4,000 m, frozen in winter and full of flowers in summer. Often combined with Gurudongmar or done on a spare day.

highlights.title: A second night to acclimatise
highlights.text: Two nights in Lachen roughly halves the shock of the Gurudongmar climb. Use the spare day for a slow walk, early sleep and plenty of water.

highlights.title: Dzumsa rules at work
highlights.text: Lachen's council sets tight rules on tourism: vehicle queues, homestay registration and limits on waste. Ask your host how the Pipon is chosen and what the village has decided about plastic.

how_to_reach.text: Most visitors join a shared 3-day tour from Gangtok: day 1 to Lachen, day 2 Gurudongmar and on to Lachung, day 3 Yumthang and back. About ₹6,000–8,000 per person with permit, rooms and meals. Book a day ahead.
A whole vehicle from a registered Gangtok operator, for ₹18,000–28,000 on the 3-day Lachen–Lachung loop before hotels. Ask for a 4-day version with two nights at Lachen.

Some tours run the loop in reverse, Lachung first, then Lachen via Chungthang, about 50 km and 2.5–3 hours. Check current status before you travel; the Chungthang–Lachen section has had the longest closures.

where_to_stay: Lachen has a few dozen small hotels and family homestays along the main road and the slope below the monastery. Shared tours assign rooms; the standard is simple, with thick quilts, hot water by bucket or geyser, and dinner and breakfast included. Ask for a heater in winter. The best budget value is in the family-run homestays, at about ₹1,500–2,500 per person with meals. Lachen's Dzumsa registers guesthouses, so book through your agent or a host you have spoken to directly.
tips: Sleep early: Gurudongmar vehicles leave at 3–4 am.
Spend two nights here if anyone in your group is older or has never been above 3,000 m.
Drink 3–4 litres of water the day before Gurudongmar and avoid alcohol.
Pack the night before and keep your down jacket and gloves on top.
Carry cash from Gangtok; Lachen has no reliable ATM.

experiences.title: Lachen Monastery and its young monks
experiences.summary: Lachen Monastery, Ngodrub Choling, is a Nyingma gompa built in 1858 above the village, with a monastic school for young monks. Walk up in the afternoon of your spare day for the view, the murals and, if you are lucky, the sound of lessons.
body: Ngodrub Choling was built in 1858, when Lachen was a herding and trading village on the route toward the Tibetan plateau. It follows the Nyingma school, like most of North Sikkim's village gompas, and it is the religious centre of Lachen. The Lachen Monastic School attached to it teaches young monks from the valley.

The walk up from the main road is steep but short, about 20–30 minutes at this height. Go slowly. From the courtyard you look down over the tin and timber roofs of Lachen and up the valley the Gurudongmar road follows. Inside are murals, statues and butter lamps; ask before taking photographs.

Afternoon is the best time, when the light is warm and you are not rushing to bed for a 3 am start. Walk clockwise, remove shoes before entering the prayer hall, and leave a small donation, ₹50–100, at the altar. Do not interrupt classes; watch from the door if the teacher allows.

faqs.q: When was Lachen Monastery built?
faqs.a: Lachen Monastery, also called Ngodrub Choling, was built in 1858. It is a Nyingma Buddhist gompa above Lachen village and is home to the Lachen Monastic School. It is the religious centre of the Lachenpa community.

faqs.q: How do I get to Lachen Monastery?
faqs.a: Walk up from Lachen's main road in about 20–30 minutes; it is steep, so go slowly at this altitude. Some vehicles can drive closer. Ask your homestay for directions. Afternoon is the best time, since most tour schedules leave no other gap.

faqs.q: Can I visit Lachen Monastery on a 1-night tour?
faqs.a: Rarely. One-night tours reach Lachen in the evening and leave for Gurudongmar at 3–4 am, then continue to Lachung. With two nights in Lachen you have the afternoon free, which is the time to visit.

experiences.title: A slow acclimatisation day in Lachen
experiences.summary: The cheapest insurance against altitude sickness at Gurudongmar is a spare day in Lachen. Walk gently along the village lanes and a short way up the valley, gain a little height, come back down to sleep, and eat and drink well.
body: Mountaineers have a simple rule: climb high, sleep low. Lachen lets you follow it. You arrive from Gangtok at around 1,700 m to 2,750 m in a day, and Gurudongmar is roughly 2,400 m above that. A rest day here gives your body time to start adjusting before the big climb.

Spend the morning walking gently: through the village, up to the monastery, along the lanes above the river. Aim to climb 200–300 m above the village and come back down. Keep the pace slow enough to talk easily. In the afternoon rest, drink water and tea, and eat a proper lunch and dinner.

Watch for early signs of altitude sickness: headache that does not go with water and rest, nausea, poor sleep or unusual tiredness. If they appear, skip Gurudongmar and go to Chopta Valley or Thangu instead, or nowhere higher at all. Some doctors advise acetazolamide; ask your own doctor before the trip, not a shopkeeper in Lachen.

faqs.q: Do I need an extra day in Lachen before Gurudongmar?
faqs.a: It is strongly advised, though most tours skip it. Gurudongmar is roughly 2,400 m higher than Lachen. With one night, the body has very little time to adjust. A spare day in Lachen reduces the risk of headaches and sickness, especially for older people and first-time visitors to high altitude.

faqs.q: What should I do on a rest day in Lachen?
faqs.a: Walk gently around the village, visit Lachen Monastery, and climb a few hundred metres before returning to sleep. Drink 3–4 litres of water, eat well and avoid alcohol and smoking. Sleep early. A visit to Chopta Valley can also be arranged if your permit includes it.

faqs.q: Should I take Diamox for Gurudongmar?
faqs.a: Ask your own doctor before the trip. Acetazolamide (sold as Diamox) is used by many to help acclimatise, but it has side effects and is not suitable for everyone. It does not replace a slow ascent. Do not take it on the advice of a driver or shopkeeper.

experiences.title: Evening in a Lachenpa kitchen
experiences.summary: Sit by the stove in your homestay kitchen before an early dinner and ask about the Dzumsa, the Pipon and winter in Lachen. Most families are glad to talk while they cook thukpa or dal, and you leave knowing how the village actually works.
body: In Lachen's cold months the kitchen is the family's sitting room, with a stove going from dusk. If you are staying in a homestay, ask politely in the afternoon if you can join while dinner is made. Most families say yes. It is the best place to understand the village, far better than the main road.

Ask about the Dzumsa: how the Pipon is chosen, what the council decided about tourism vehicles and homestays, and why the village is careful about waste. Ask about the summer herds at Thangu, about the 2023 flood and the closed road, and about children going to school in Mangan or Gangtok. Listen more than you talk.

Food will be simple: rice, dal, a vegetable, perhaps meat or eggs, and tea. Thukpa or thenthuk may appear on cold nights. Eat early, by 7.30 pm, because you will be up at 3 am for Gurudongmar. Do not ask for alcohol, and if offered home brew, decline politely before the high drive.

faqs.q: What is the Pipon in Lachen?
faqs.a: The Pipon is the elected headman of Lachen's Dzumsa, the traditional council in which every household is represented. The Pipon chairs meetings, settles disputes and speaks for the village. Lachung has its own Pipon and Dzumsa. The system dates from the first half of the 19th century.

faqs.q: What food is served in Lachen homestays?
faqs.a: Simple home food: rice, dal, a vegetable such as potato or radish, eggs and sometimes chicken, with tea. On cold nights you may get thukpa or thenthuk noodle soup. Dinner and breakfast are usually included. Tell your host about dietary needs when you arrive.

faqs.q: Can I drink alcohol in Lachen before Gurudongmar?
faqs.a: It is best not to. Alcohol dehydrates you and makes altitude sickness more likely and harder to spot. With a 3–4 am start for a lake at about 5,180 m, a clear head and a full night's sleep matter more. Save it for Gangtok.

experiences.title: Green Lake: the restricted Zemu trek
experiences.cost: Special permits and a full trekking crew; ask agents
experiences.summary: From Lachen a long trail runs up the Zemu valley toward Green Lake and the north-east face of Kanchenjunga. It needs special permission, a licensed agency and a full crew. We describe it so you can ask the right questions, not as a weekend option.
body: The Zemu Glacier, one of the largest in the eastern Himalaya, flows from Kanchenjunga toward the Lachen valley. Early climbers approached Kanchenjunga from this side, and the Green Lake area near the glacier gives a view of the mountain's north-east face. The route lies within or near Khangchendzonga National Park, and Siniolchu rises above it.

The trek starts near Lachen and takes roughly 8–12 days return, through forest and then high moraine above 4,000 m. It is a serious expedition-style walk. Indian nationals and foreigners need special permission beyond the normal North Sikkim permit, and only registered agencies can arrange it. Permission has been granted in some seasons and not in others.

If you want to do it, start with registered Gangtok trekking agencies months in advance, budget for guides, porters or pack animals, food and camping gear, and expect a cost many times higher than a shared tour. Since the 2023 flood the approach roads have also been unreliable. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Can I trek to Green Lake from Lachen?
faqs.a: Only with special permission arranged by a registered agency, in seasons when it is granted. The trek runs up the Zemu valley toward the Zemu Glacier and the north-east face of Kanchenjunga, taking about 8–12 days. It is not covered by the normal North Sikkim tour permit. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How hard is the Green Lake trek?
faqs.a: It is a long, high trek with several days above 4,000 m on moraine and rough ground. You need good fitness, previous high-altitude trekking experience and a full support crew. It is not a trek for beginners, and weather can close the route.

faqs.q: How much does the Green Lake trek cost?
faqs.a: We cannot give a reliable figure, because it depends on permission fees, group size, crew and season, and few agencies run it each year. Expect it to cost many times a standard North Sikkim tour. Ask several registered Gangtok trekking agencies for written quotes.

faqs.q: How far is Lachen from Gangtok?
faqs.a: Lachen is about 129 km north of Gangtok by road, via Mangan and Chungthang. Before 2023 the drive took about six hours; with flood repairs and diversions it often takes 6–8 hours now, and the Chungthang–Lachen section has had long closures. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Why do Gurudongmar tours stay in Lachen?
faqs.a: Lachen is the last village with tourist rooms on the road to Gurudongmar, about 65 km and three hours below the lake. Staying here lets you leave at 3–4 am, reach the lake in the clear morning and be back down before wind and cloud build up around midday.

faqs.q: What is the altitude of Lachen?
faqs.a: Lachen is at roughly 2,750 m, with sources giving figures from about 2,700 m to 2,900 m. Nights are cold year-round and well below freezing in winter. Most people sleep fine at this height but may feel slightly breathless climbing the village lanes.

faqs.q: Is Lachen open for tourists now?
faqs.a: It depends on the month. Since the October 2023 Teesta flood, the road from Chungthang to Lachen has opened and closed several times, and tours to Lachen and Gurudongmar have been suspended for long periods. Ask your Gangtok agent and the Mangan district administration, and check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Can foreigners stay in Lachen?
faqs.a: Rules have varied. Foreign nationals have sometimes been allowed to Lachen with a Protected Area Permit through a registered agent, but not to Gurudongmar. The list changes, so ask your agent which places your permit covers, and check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What is there to do in Lachen besides Gurudongmar?
faqs.a: Visit Lachen Monastery, built in 1858; walk the village lanes; take a day to Chopta Valley and Thangu; and talk to your hosts about the Dzumsa council. With a spare day you can rest and acclimatise, which makes Gurudongmar safer and more enjoyable.

faqs.q: How cold is Lachen in winter?
faqs.a: Very cold. Winter nights often drop to −5 to −10 °C, and days are close to freezing in the shade. Snow can fall from December to March. Bring thermals, a down jacket, warm cap and gloves, and ask for a room with a heater.

faqs.q: Are there ATMs in Lachen?
faqs.a: Do not count on one. Carry all the cash you need for your North Sikkim tour from Gangtok, plus a margin for delays or extras. Mangan, the district headquarters, has several banks. Digital payments work only when the network does, which is patchy.

faqs.q: What does a Lachen homestay cost?
faqs.a: About ₹1,500–2,500 per person per night with dinner and breakfast, booked directly or through a Gangtok agent. On a shared tour your room and meals are included in the package price. Rates rise in May, October and late December.
